title: Logging and monitoring: which logs do you need, and which alerts deserve a person?
short: Send identity, cloud and server logs to a store your admins can't erase, keep 12 months and prove monthly that your alerts fire.
answer: This month, send Entra, Microsoft 365, cloud and server logs to a store that your everyday admin accounts can't change or delete, and keep 12 months of them, the first 6 searchable, as the new US federal baseline requires[^m2614]. Then alert on the few events that are rarely harmless, give each alert a named owner and deputy, and prove every month that the alerts still reach them.
audience: IT and security teams in small and mid-size organizations without a 24/7 SOC, many on Microsoft 365 and Entra ID with some on-premises servers and cloud workloads

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Get logs out of their default stores.
items.text: Entra keeps sign-in and audit logs 7 days on Free and 30 on P1 or P2[^entraret]; the Azure Activity log[^activity] and CloudTrail event history[^ctbp] keep 90 days. Export each one this month.

items.title: Keep the copy where your admins can't delete it.
items.text: Attackers delete local logs to hide[^asd]. Use a separate Azure subscription or AWS account with its own admins[^ctbp], on immutable storage that even account administrators can't delete[^immutable].

items.title: Turn on the Windows logging that's off by default.
items.text: Enable **Audit Process Creation** with command lines[^cmdline] and **PowerShell Script Block Logging**[^pslog], plus at least the minimum audit policy for Windows Event Forwarding[^wef].

items.title: Name who answers each alert.
items.text: Send alerts to a shared mailbox and a phone, with a named person and deputy each week. If nobody answers at night, pay a managed detection service before buying tools.

items.title: Alert when a source goes quiet, and test monthly.
items.text: Alert on unexpected log termination, as Mandiant advises[^mtrends]. Monthly, run Defender for Endpoint's detection test on a server, whose alert appears in about 10 minutes[^mdetest], and check that a person saw it.

blocks.title: Check whether your logging would hold up

items.title: Could you see an admin sign-in from 10 months ago?
items.text: If not, extend retention. It can take up to 18 months to discover an incident[^asd], and Mandiant calls standard 90-day retention insufficient for scoping intrusions[^mtrends].

items.title: Who could erase the central copy?
items.text: List every account that can delete logs or stop collection. If any of them is an everyday admin account, separate the store.

items.title: Do all clocks agree?
items.text: Point the PDC emulator in the forest root at a reliable external source; domain members follow the domain hierarchy[^w32time]. Store timestamps in UTC as ISO 8601 and use more than one time source[^asd].

items.title: Is every planned source arriving?
items.text: Compare the asset list with the sources that sent data this week. The BSI's federal standard requires this check after rollout, including data formats and time sync[^bsipd].

items.title: When did an alert last reach someone after hours?
items.text: If nobody knows, raise a test alert on a Sunday evening and time the response.

blocks.title: Logs to collect first
items: **Rank by what attackers want.** ASD and its partners rank critical systems and data first, then internet-facing services, identity servers, other critical servers, edge devices and admin workstations[^asd].

**Entra ID and Microsoft 365.** Export sign-in logs, including non-interactive and service principal sign-ins, audit logs and Graph activity logs[^entralogs], which aren't kept unless exported[^entraret]. The incident response sheet covers the unified audit log.
**Linux.** Load audit rules from `/usr/share/audit/sample-rules` with `augenrules --load`[^rhaudit], and log use of curl, systemctl and python[^asd].

**Cloud.** In AWS, use a multi-Region trail with log file integrity validation[^ctbp]. In Azure, add an Activity log diagnostic setting per subscription; a management group setting misses some events[^activity].
**Edge devices and hypervisors.** See the edge devices sheet. Mandiant calls hypervisor logs the only way to detect snapshot tampering or rogue virtual machines[^mtrends].

blocks.title: Alerts worth a person's time
items: **Logging stopped or cleared.** Windows events 1102 and 104 mean a log was cleared[^wef]. Also alert on deleted diagnostic settings and stopped trails.
**New admin rights.** Use the privileged access sheet's list for AD groups and Entra roles. For edge devices, see the edge devices sheet.
**Mail forwarded outside.** The default policy **Suspicious email forwarding activity** is High severity and on by default in E1, E3 and E5[^alertpol]. Add your alert mailbox as a recipient.
**Security tools changed.** Alert when someone changes Defender or logging settings or disables monitoring services[^asd].
**High-severity incidents.** Create a Defender XDR email rule for High and Medium incidents and use **Send test email**[^xdrmail].
**Large data exports.** ASD advises alerting on large or continuous exports by default[^asd].

blocks.title: Retention and cost
items: **Keep 12 months, 6 of them searchable.** That's the US federal minimum since May 2026[^m2614], and a sound default.
**Tier the storage.** Keep recent logs hot and older ones cold[^asd]. Sentinel retains analytics data free for 90 days and offers a cheaper lake tier for bulky tables[^sentbill].
**Start with what's free.** Sentinel ingests Azure Activity, Office 365 audit logs and Defender alerts free; raw Entra ID and Defender logs cost extra[^sentbill].
**Filter at the source.** Collect Windows security events with the Common or Minimal set, and keep non-security data in a separate workspace[^sentcost].

**Write the period down.** NIS2 entities must keep logs for a predefined period[^enisa]. The BSI suggests 90 days for federal log data but lets security events without personal data stay longer[^bsipd].

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **The US federal baseline was cut back.** OMB's M-26-14 of 22 May 2026 replaced M-21-31, whose retention of vast amounts of log data proved neither feasible nor cost-effective for most agencies[^m2614].

**CISA published a logging reference architecture.** Its August 2026 guide lists health and completeness monitoring, synthetic tests and automated threat emulation as features a logging system needs[^lra].
**CISA retired Logging Made Easy.** Support ended on 22 May 2026 and the repository is read-only[^lme]. If you run it, plan a replacement.
**Sysmon is built into Windows.** Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025 include it as an optional feature. Uninstall standalone Sysmon first, and parse the XML, as event text is now localized[^sysmon].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Sending everything to the SIEM.** CISA notes that SIEM-first designs often become costly as volume grows[^lra]. Keep bulky logs in cheaper storage.
**Microsoft service principal sign-in logs.** Microsoft calls this preview log high-volume and not essential for security investigations[^entralogs].
**Data access logs everywhere.** Google Cloud leaves them off, except for BigQuery, because of their volume[^gcpaudit]. Enable them only for sensitive data.
**Hundreds of imported rules.** Ten alerts that someone answers beat hundreds that nobody reads.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Basic audit policy overwriting the advanced one.** Enable **Audit: Force audit policy subcategory settings**; event 4719 shows an overwrite[^cmdline].
**Local logs too small.** Windows Event Forwarding buffers in the local log, and events overwritten while the collector is unreachable are lost without notice[^wef]. Raise maximum log sizes[^asd].
**Expecting a license upgrade to bring back history.** Entra retention changes aren't retroactive; expired data is gone unless you archived it[^entraret].
**Letting everyone read the logs.** Command lines and script blocks can expose passwords and other credentials[^cmdline][^pslog]. Limit who can read them.

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Turn on Defender XDR incident emails for High and Medium severity to a shared mailbox[^xdrmail].
Archive Entra logs to a storage account in its own subscription with a locked immutability policy[^immutable].
Ask your IT provider for the last alert it acted on and how long that took.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Run one SIEM workspace: free sources first, then Entra sign-ins and server security events.
Write one rule per item in the alert list, each with an owner, and test them monthly.
Cover nights and weekends with a managed detection service that may isolate devices.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: NIS2 cloud, data center and managed service providers must sync clocks and monitor logging availability independently[^enisa].
Keep a year or more in a cheaper lake tier and only recent data in analytics[^sentbill].
Inject synthetic events per source category and track failures to a fix[^lra].
